_provenance.citation: Huyghues-Despointes, B.M.P., Scholtz, J.M. & Baldwin, R.L. (1993). Effect of a single aspartate on helix stability at different positions in a neutral alanine-based peptide. Protein Sci. 2, 1604-1611.
_provenance.doi_note: No DOI printed in the copy under doc/ (Cambridge University Press, 1993). Left null rather than supplied from memory. The citation itself is now VERIFIED: the paper's own first page prints 'Protein Science (1993), 2, 1604-1611'.
_provenance.attribution_resolved: RESOLVED at cycle 60. The provenance block previously warned that a DIFFERENT Huyghues-Despointes/Scholtz/Baldwin 1993 Protein Sci. paper ('Helical peptides with three pairs of Asp-Arg and Glu-Arg residues in different orientations and spacings', 2, 80-85) might be the real source. Both papers are now under doc/. This one is correct: its reference peptide is Ac-(AAQAA)3Y-NH2 and its Figure 1 is a scan of a single Asp over positions 1-16, which is exactly this dataset. The Asp-Arg/Glu-Arg paper contains no such scan.
_provenance.temperature_source: "A: Dependence of helix content on position of Asp0 at pH 2 in 10 mM NaCl at 0 °C. ... B: Dependence of helix content on position of Asp- at pH 7.0 in 10 mM NaCl at 0 °C." (legend to Figure 1). Also Methods: "The degree of helical structure in each peptide was determined by monitoring the ellipticity at 222 nm at 0 °C." The previously coded 0.0 was correct.
_provenance.ionic_strength_source: "...at pH 2 in 10 mM NaCl at 0 °C" / "...at pH 7.0 in 10 mM NaCl at 0 °C" (legend to Figure 1). The previously coded 0.01 was correct as the stated salt.
_provenance.ionic_strength_derivation: The stated 10 mM NaCl is coded exactly. It is a LOWER BOUND on the true I: Methods add buffer -- "prepared by diluting aqueous stock solutions into 10 mM NaCl buffered with 1 mM sodium citrate, 1 mM sodium phosphate, and 1 mM sodium borate (CD buffer)" -- and the pH was set per sample. At pH 7 the citrate (pKa3 6.4) is largely trivalent and contributes ~5 mM to I on its own; at pH 2 the ~10 mM HCl needed to reach that pH contributes ~10 mM. Estimated true I is ~17 mM at pH 7 and ~22 mM at pH 2, i.e. 1.7-2.2x the coded value, and pH-dependent in the same way Lacroix's is. Coding the stated salt keeps the value traceable to a quote; the sensitivity of the model to the difference was measured at cycle 60 (see reasoning/nodes/N046.md) and found to be small for this dataset.
